decisionsTitle: Race results, part 4: a race's own age categories, and the podium for the awards
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-24, from the phone:** «I need to be able to create sex and age group categories for winners in order to give awards.» The ranking already placed every finisher by sex and by category (§808), but the category was one fixed table — the statistics' bands of §787, ten years wide from eighteen — and the podium had to be read off the whole sheet.

**Decision, the categories.** A category stays what §808 made it, the sex and an age band on the race's day; what a race may now choose is **where its bands start**: `events.result_age_bands` (migration `0178`, an expand — one nullable jsonb column), an ascending list of one to twelve ages between 1 and 99, read through `results/domain/age-bands.ts#ageBandStartsOf`. Null is the platform's bands, `DEFAULT_AGE_BAND_STARTS` = `[18, 30, 40, 50, 60]`, so every race that exists ranks exactly as before and the stored keys (`FEMALE:from30`, `MALE:under18`) keep their shape — a key says only where a band begins, and its end is read from the race's list, so the same `from30` reads «30-39 ani» under the platform's bands and «30-44 ani» where the next band starts at 45 (`bandLabelOf`). The catalogue's six fixed band words became three sentences with placeholders («sub {age} ani», «{from}-{to} ani», «{from}+ ani»), filled per band; the statistics' footer fills them from the platform's list and reads as it did. The box «Categorii de vârstă» sits on «Clasament», a form of its own (`setResultAgeBands`): whoever enters results may set it (the Organizer too), the list is read in any order and sorted, an empty box forgets the choice (null, never a copy of the default), a box that cannot be read is refused in place naming the problem (`RESULTS_AGE_BANDS`), and a change **ranks the stored results again in the same transaction** and tells the public cache, so a place by category never describes a band the race no longer has. One audit row, `event_results.categories_changed`, carries the ages and how many rows moved, never a runner. The public read carries the race's bands (`PublicEventResults.ageBandStarts`), so the event page, the CSV and the filter's chips say each category in the race's own words; the chips sort by the age a band starts at, whatever the bands.

**Decision, the podium.** «Premii», a card on «Clasament» (`results/domain/awards.ts#awardsOf`, pure): women then men, each sex's overall podium first — the ranking's own position by sex — then its categories youngest band first, the first three places in each (`AWARD_PLACES`), a tie on the same step, a group with nobody placed left out. Each line is the number, the name as the backoffice sees it and the gun time; nothing is counted again here and nothing is stored. The card is for the organizers at the ceremony; the public page is unchanged, since each public row already carries its place in its category.

**Refused.** Named categories typed by the club (`M35`, `Veterani`): the sex and the start age say the same with nothing to translate and nothing to keep consistent between two languages. A category by sex alone or by age alone: the positions by sex exist already, and an age-only podium would mix the two sexes the club awards apart. Per-event places count: three is the podium; a race that awards more reads the places on the lines. Carrying the bands with a duplicate, a repeat or the JSON file: the next race decides its own categories, as it decides its results (§808's rule for `results_published`). Changing the Excel's «Statistici» to each event's bands: the Excel counts every event under one table so its totals compare; it keeps the platform's groups and SETUP.md §45 says so.
changelogLine: - **A race chooses its own age categories, and «Clasament» shows the podium** — «Categorii de vârstă» on the results page takes the ages each group starts at («18, 35, 45, 55»), ranks the saved results again under them and says them on the event page, in the CSV and in the filter; «Premii» lists the first three places for women, for men and in every category, from the saved results, for the awards. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a race's «Clasament» page, when an Organizer or an Administrator writes the ages the age groups start at in «Categorii de vârstă» and presses «Salvează categoriile», then the list (one to twelve whole ages between 1 and 99, read in any order and sorted, an empty box meaning the platform's bands 18, 30, 40, 50, 60 stored as null) is saved on the event, every stored result is ranked again by category in the same transaction, one audit row records the ages and how many rows moved and never a runner, the public cache is told, a list that cannot be read is refused in place naming the problem with every box keeping what was typed, on an event that is not a race it is refused RESULTS_NOT_OPEN, and the Tehnic role, the Redactor, the desk Volunteer and a member are refused FORBIDDEN whatever the page drew (2026-10-24, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `results/age-bands.test.ts`, `results/ranking.test.ts`, integration `results/results.test.ts`, `results/actions.test.ts`, `results/page.test.ts`.

Given a race's saved results, when its «Clasament» page is drawn, then a card «Premii» lists, from the ranking's own positions and counting nothing again, the first three places by sex for women then for men and the first three in each of the race's categories youngest band first, each line the race number, the name as the backoffice sees it and the gun time, a tie on the same step and a group with nobody placed left out; and a category is said in words from the race's own bands — the same stored key reading «30-39 ani» under the platform's bands and «30-44 ani» where the next band starts at 45 — on that page, on the event page, in the CSV and on the filter's chips, which sort by the age a band starts at (2026-10-24, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `results/awards.test.ts`, `results/age-bands.test.ts`, `results/csv-and-words.test.ts`, integration `results/page.test.ts`, `results/results.test.ts`.
